content_summary: SEBI's Board approved establishing a regulatory framework for ESG Rating Providers by inserting a new chapter into the SEBI (Credit Rating Agencies) Regulations, 1999, rather than a standalone accreditation-only scheme. The adopted framework created two tiers -- Category I and Category II ERPs -- with different net-worth and service-scope criteria, open to a wider pool of applicants than the CRA/RA-only eligibility proposed in the Jan 2022 anchor paper. It introduced a requirement that ERPs consider India/Emerging-Market parameters, a 'Core ESG Rating' tied to assured BRSR Core data, and (per the intervening Feb 2023 consultation paper that fed the Board decision) allowed either an issuer-pays or a subscriber-pays model rather than mandating subscriber-pay as originally proposed.

key_parameters.name: entities eligible for ERP status
key_parameters.proposed: Only SEBI-registered Credit Rating Agencies and Research Analysts (Jan 2022 paper)
key_parameters.final: Any entity meeting Category I or Category II registration criteria under a new CRA Regulations chapter -- not limited to existing CRAs/RAs

key_parameters.name: minimum net worth
key_parameters.proposed: Flat Rs. 10 crore (in addition to existing CRA/RA net worth)
key_parameters.final: Category I: liquid net worth >= Rs. 5 crore ongoing / Rs. 10 crore at application; Category II: >= Rs. 10 lakh ongoing / Rs. 20 lakh at application

key_parameters.name: ERP business/payment model
key_parameters.proposed: Mandatory subscriber-pay
key_parameters.final: Either issuer-pays or subscriber-pays permitted (hybrid disallowed)

notes: The Jan 2022 anchor was an early concept paper; a fuller follow-on consultation (Feb 22, 2023, evidence E02) with the Category I/II structure preceded the Board's Mar 29, 2023 approval, whose PR is used as decisive_date (earliest official adoption per protocol). The SEBI (Credit Rating Agencies) (Amendment) Regulations, 2023 gazette notification followed later; not separately re-verified since it postdates the board PR and cannot be an earlier decisive date. content_label_confidence=medium: structure (Cat I/II, net worth) verified from board-meeting agenda note; business-model parameter inferred from the intervening Feb-2023 CP, not independently re-checked against the final Master Circular text.

content_summary: At its Dec 20, 2022 meeting, the SEBI Board approved amendments to the Buy-back Regulations, 2018 that reduced the buyback-tender-offer timeline by 18 days -- going beyond the consultation paper's proposed mechanism by removing the draft-letter-of-offer filing/SEBI-observation step entirely (rather than merely shortening it from T+10 to T+5) and compressing the tendering/payment period. This was formally notified via the SEBI (Buy-Back of Securities) (Amendment) Regulations, 2023 (gazetted Feb 7, 2023, effective Mar 9, 2023). The Dec 20, 2022 board press release, searched in full, contains no mention of a matching amendment to Open Offer timelines under the Takeover Regulations, 2011 -- i.e., as far as verified, the paper's other proposal (62 to 42 working days for open offers) was not acted on by the same decisive document.

key_parameters.name: buyback tender-offer completion timeline
key_parameters.proposed: 43 working days reduced to 36 working days, largely via shortening (not removing) the draft-letter-of-offer step
key_parameters.final: Reduced by 18 working days by eliminating the draft-letter-of-offer/SEBI-observation requirement altogether, plus a shorter tendering/payment period

key_parameters.name: open offer completion timeline (Takeover Regulations)
key_parameters.proposed: 62 working days reduced to 42 working days
key_parameters.final: Not confirmed adopted in the Dec 20, 2022 board decision or any other document found before censor date

notes: decisive_date uses the earliest official adopting document (board PR, Dec 20 2022) per protocol, ahead of the Feb 7 2023 gazette notification of the same amendments. content_label_confidence lowered because the open-offer/Takeover-Regulations half of the anchor's proposal could not be confirmed adopted (a targeted search found no matching SAST timeline amendment); it may simply not have been located, or may remain unresolved -- flagged rather than guessed.

content_summary: At its Sep 30, 2022 meeting, the SEBI Board approved amending the PIT Regulations, 2015 to include a separate chapter covering mutual fund units, matching the anchor proposal's core mechanism: definitions of UPSI/generally-available-information for MF units, a separate code of conduct for designated persons of AMCs/Trustees, and reporting/monitoring requirements for their MF-unit transactions. The formal amendment regulations followed (notified Nov 24, 2022 per secondary reporting), with implementation circulars issued later (including one dated Oct 22, 2024 streamlining compliance timelines, which postdates this thread's decisive action and is not used as evidence).

key_parameters.name: mechanism
key_parameters.proposed: Separate chapter in PIT Regulations, 2015 covering MF units with UPSI/connected-person/designated-person definitions
key_parameters.final: Board approved the same mechanism: 'a separate chapter' for MF units with the definitions, code of conduct and reporting/monitoring requirements as proposed

notes: Board PR text closely tracks the consultation paper's own proposed mechanism (separate chapter, MF-specific definitions, code of conduct, reporting). Did not independently diff every numeric threshold (e.g. contra-trade window, holding-disclosure thresholds) between the paper and the final gazetted amendment text, hence content_label_confidence is medium rather than high.

content_summary: At its Dec 20, 2022 meeting (the same meeting that decided IN-SEBI-H-0002), the SEBI Board approved enhancing the scope of the 'green debt security' definition to include new modes such as pollution prevention/control and eco-efficient products, and approved introducing 'blue bonds' (water/marine) and 'yellow bonds' (solar) as sub-categories of green debt securities -- both explicitly floated as questions in the anchor consultation paper. The Board also approved a 'transition bonds' sub-category, which was not explicitly named in the anchor paper's own text (an addition beyond what was asked), and directed that basic dos-and-don'ts be specified to address greenwashing risk, matching the paper's third proposal.

key_parameters.name: coloured-bond sub-categories
key_parameters.proposed: Blue bonds definitely proposed; yellow bonds raised as an open question
key_parameters.final: Blue bonds, yellow bonds AND transition bonds all approved as sub-categories of green debt securities

key_parameters.name: greenwashing safeguards
key_parameters.proposed: Reduce compliance cost 'while not creating perverse incentives that may lead to greenwashing' (general principle, no detail)
key_parameters.final: SEBI to specify 'basic dos and don'ts relating to green debt securities' to address greenwashing risk

notes: Board PR text closely mirrors the consultation paper's three stated aims (amplify green-debt-security definition, introduce blue/coloured bonds, address greenwashing); classified as_proposed despite the extra 'transition bonds' category because that addition is incremental rather than a different mechanism. Did not verify the formal NCS Regulations amendment/circular text implementing this board decision.

content_summary: At its Mar 29, 2023 meeting (the same meeting decisive for IN-SEBI-H-0001), the SEBI Board approved amendments to the LODR Regulations introducing a quantitative materiality threshold and a stricter 12-hour disclosure timeline for events emanating from within the listed entity, matching the anchor paper's core proposals. The Board additionally approved a 30-minute timeline for board-meeting-decision disclosures and a market-rumour verification/confirmation duty for top 100/250 listed entities -- provisions not present in this thread's anchor paper (they trace to the companion Feb 2023 LODR consultation and related work). Formal notification followed as the SEBI (LODR) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2023, reported effective mid-2023.

key_parameters.name: materiality threshold
key_parameters.proposed: Lower of 2% of turnover, 2% of net worth, or 5% of 3-yr avg PAT
key_parameters.final: Quantitative threshold for materiality introduced (Board PR confirms the concept; exact final percentages not independently re-verified against gazette text)

key_parameters.name: disclosure timeline (events emanating from the entity)
key_parameters.proposed: Reduced from 24 hours to 12 hours
key_parameters.final: 12 hours confirmed by Board PR, plus an additional 30-minute timeline for board-meeting decisions not present in the anchor proposal

notes: Board PR section 10.1 tracks the anchor's two central asks (quantitative threshold, 12-hour timeline) almost verbatim. Did not independently verify the exact final materiality-threshold percentages against the gazetted LODR (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2023 text, hence content_label_confidence is medium.

content_summary: At its Mar 29, 2023 meeting (the same meeting decisive for IN-SEBI-H-0001 and IN-SEBI-H-0005), the SEBI Board approved harnessing Online Dispute Resolution by: extending the MII-administered conciliation/arbitration mechanism to registered intermediaries/regulated entities and their investors/clients; conducting proceedings in hybrid mode; expanding the MII mechanism's capacity with the aid of ODR institutions; and streamlining the dispute-resolution process and enforcement of awards -- closely matching the anchor paper's two central proposals (online, ODR-institution-assisted process; extension to all intermediaries).

key_parameters.name: mechanism
key_parameters.proposed: Make MII-administered mediation/conciliation/arbitration fully online via ODR institutions; extend to all specified intermediaries
key_parameters.final: Board approved extending the MII mechanism to registered intermediaries/regulated entities, hybrid-mode proceedings, ODR-institution-assisted capacity expansion, and streamlined enforcement

notes: Board PR section 16 mirrors the anchor CP's language and structure closely (online/hybrid ODR-assisted mechanism, extension to all intermediaries). Did not verify the implementing circular's operational detail (e.g. whether appellate arbitration was in fact removed, or the sole-mediator provision adopted as proposed), hence content_label_confidence is medium.

content_summary: At its Mar 29, 2023 meeting (the same meeting decisive for several other threads in this sample), the SEBI Board approved amendments to the MF Regulations, 1996 that, while strengthening the existing sponsor eligibility criteria, introduced an alternative route enabling a diverse set of entities -- explicitly including private equity funds, with safeguards -- to become MF sponsors, and allowed 'Self Sponsored AMCs' to continue the business (letting the original sponsor voluntarily disassociate without inducting a new sponsor). This matches the anchor paper's two central proposals almost verbatim. The amendment to the MF Regulations followed on June 26, 2023, with an implementing circular on July 7, 2023 (per secondary reporting; not independently fetched here as it postdates the decisive board action).

key_parameters.name: alternate eligibility route
key_parameters.proposed: Allow entities lacking the 5-year profitability track record (incl. Private Equity funds) to sponsor an MF, subject to higher net worth
key_parameters.final: Board approved the alternate route explicitly for a 'diverse set of entities... include private equity funds, with requisite safeguards'

key_parameters.name: self-sponsored structure
key_parameters.proposed: 'Self-Sponsored AMC' concept letting a mature AMC continue without a distinct sponsor once qualifying conditions are met
key_parameters.final: Board approved 'Self Sponsored AMCs' to continue the MF business, letting the original sponsor voluntarily disassociate

notes: Board PR paragraph 9 tracks the anchor paper's proposal structure and even its terminology ('Self Sponsored AMCs', 'alternative route', private equity funds) very closely. Did not fetch the June 26, 2023 gazette amendment or July 2023 circular to verify exact final net-worth figures against the paper's discussed options, hence content_label_confidence is medium.

decisive_document_title: Direct plan for schemes of Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) and trail model for distribution commission in AIFs
content_summary: SEBI issued circular SEBI/HO/AFD/PoD/CIR/2023/054 on April 10, 2023, prescribing exactly the two proposed mechanisms: a mandatory no-fee 'direct plan' for AIF investors coming through a separately-fee-charging intermediary, and a trail-based distribution-commission model -- fully trail for Category III AIFs, and trail with up to one-third payable upfront in year one for Category I/II AIFs. Applicable to investors onboarded from May 1, 2023.

key_parameters.name: direct plan mandate
key_parameters.proposed: AIFs must offer a no-distribution-fee direct plan; mandatory for investors already paying a separate advisory/PM fee
key_parameters.final: Adopted as proposed per the April 2023 circular

key_parameters.name: distribution commission model
key_parameters.proposed: Cat III: pure trail; Cat I/II: trail with up to 1/3 of PV of total fee payable upfront in year 1
key_parameters.final: Adopted as proposed: Cat III equal trail basis (no upfront); Cat I/II up to one-third upfront, remainder on equal trail basis

notes: No board-meeting press release was found preceding this circular; AIPAC had already recommended both proposals before the consultation paper was published, and SEBI appears to have moved straight from consultation to circular. Content match confirmed via secondary summaries of the April 10, 2023 circular's operative paragraphs, not the full circular PDF text itself, hence content_label_confidence is medium.

content_summary: At its Mar 29, 2023 meeting, the SEBI Board approved (item 15.4) mandating 75%-investor-by-value approval for AIF purchases/sales of investments involving conflict of interest, covering transactions with associates or affiliated AIF schemes exactly as proposed -- but the Board additionally extended the same 75% consent requirement to transactions with 'an investor who has commitment to the extent of more than 50% of the corpus of the scheme of AIF', a category not present in the anchor consultation paper. Formal notification followed via the SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2023 (~mid-June 2023) and related circulars (~June 21, 2023).

key_parameters.name: consent threshold
key_parameters.proposed: 75% of investors by value
key_parameters.final: 75% of investors by value (unchanged)

key_parameters.name: covered counterparties
key_parameters.proposed: Associates of the AIF; schemes of AIFs managed/sponsored by the Manager, Sponsor or their associates
key_parameters.final: Same two categories, PLUS any investor holding more than 50% of the scheme's corpus -- an added category beyond the anchor proposal

notes: Board PR paragraph 15.4 restates the anchor's 75%-consent mechanism almost verbatim, then explicitly adds the >50%-corpus-investor category, which is why this is coded 'tightened' rather than 'as_proposed'. Did not verify the June 2023 gazette/circular text itself.

content_summary: At its Mar 29, 2023 meeting, the SEBI Board approved introducing the GID/KID concept for non-convertible securities and Commercial Paper substantially as proposed (GID filed at first issuance, valid one year; KID for subsequent issuances; a common schedule aligning public-issue and private-placement disclosures) -- but the Board PR states the concept 'is proposed to be made applicable on a comply-or-explain basis till March 31, 2024 and mandatory thereafter', a phased/softer rollout than the anchor paper's proposal, which did not include a comply-or-explain grace period. Formal notification followed via the NCS (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2023, gazetted July 6, 2023.

key_parameters.name: GID/KID mechanism
key_parameters.proposed: One-year-valid GID plus a shorter KID for subsequent issuances, replacing repeated placement memoranda
key_parameters.final: Adopted as proposed structurally, but phased in on a comply-or-explain basis until March 31, 2024 before becoming mandatory

key_parameters.name: disclosure parity
key_parameters.proposed: Align private-placement disclosures with public-issue prospectus disclosures
key_parameters.final: Adopted: a common schedule for both public issue and private placement disclosures

notes: Corrected during QA: the earliest official adopting document is the Mar 29, 2023 board PR (item 12), not the Jul 6, 2023 gazette amendment which only formalizes it. The board PR's own text reveals a comply-or-explain transition period not present in the Feb 2023 anchor consultation paper, hence 'softened' rather than 'as_proposed'.

content_summary: At its Mar 29, 2023 meeting (the same meeting decisive for several other threads in this sample), the SEBI Board approved ICDR amendments including: disclosure of underwriting for shortfall/subscription-risk coverage in the offer document prior to issue opening; and the bonus-issue precondition (stock-exchange approval for listing/trading of all pre-bonus securities) plus mandatory dematerialised-form bonus issuance. The Board PR (which says amendments were approved 'inter alia' on these issues) does not explicitly confirm the anchor's other two proposals (pension-fund Anchor Investor eligibility; expanded offer-document inspection/website-hosting disclosures).

key_parameters.name: underwriting disclosure
key_parameters.proposed: Disclose underwriting for shortfall/subscription-risk coverage in the offer document prior to issue opening
key_parameters.final: Adopted as proposed per Board PR 11.1

key_parameters.name: bonus issue precondition
key_parameters.proposed: Bonus announcement only after stock-exchange approval for listing/trading of all pre-bonus securities; demat-only bonus issuance
key_parameters.final: Adopted as proposed per Board PR 11.2

notes: Board PR item 11 explicitly confirms items (a) and (b) of the anchor's four-part proposal in near-identical language; items (c) (pension-fund anchor investors) and (d) (offer-document inspection/website disclosures) are not mentioned in the PR's 'inter alia' summary, so their adoption status is unconfirmed as of this decisive document (they may have been included in the underlying gazette text without a PR callout, or dropped) -- flagged rather than assumed either way.

content_summary: At its June 28, 2023 meeting, the SEBI Board approved (item 4) that the Sponsor of an InvIT/REIT be required to hold a minimum unitholding 'on a reducing scale for the entire life of the InvIT/REIT', with the mandatory minimum unitholding locked-in and unencumbered -- matching the anchor's core mechanism (declining-scale perpetual holding, unencumbered). The Board additionally introduced a 'Self-Sponsored Investment Manager/Manager' concept for InvITs/REITs and board nomination rights for unitholders, which were bundled into the same agenda item but are not part of this thread's anchor proposal.

key_parameters.name: minimum sponsor unitholding
key_parameters.proposed: Declining scale: 15% (<=3yr), 5% (3-5yr), 3% (5-10yr), 2% (10-20yr), 1% (>20yr), unencumbered
key_parameters.final: Board approved a 'reducing scale for the entire life' of the vehicle, locked-in and unencumbered -- consistent with the proposed mechanism (exact final percentages not independently re-verified against gazette text)

notes: Board PR item 4.2 uses language ('reducing scale for the entire life', 'locked-in and unencumbered') that closely tracks the anchor's proposed mechanism. Did not verify the exact final percentage schedule against the subsequent gazette amendment, hence content_label_confidence is medium rather than high.

content_summary: At its June 28, 2023 meeting (the same meeting decisive for IN-SEBI-H-0012), the SEBI Board approved amendments to the InvIT and REIT Regulations to provide nomination rights to unitholders holding 10% or more of total outstanding units, individually or collectively, on the board of the Investment Manager/Manager, and applied Stewardship Code principles to such unitholders -- matching the anchor's 'Option 1' proposal (10% threshold, collective clubbing, Stewardship Code) essentially verbatim. The Board PR does not mention the alternative 'Unitholder Council' option, indicating Option 1 was the one adopted.

key_parameters.name: nomination-right threshold
key_parameters.proposed: 10% of outstanding units, individually or collectively (clubbing allowed for smaller holders)
key_parameters.final: 10% of total outstanding units, individually or collectively -- adopted as proposed

key_parameters.name: Stewardship Code applicability
key_parameters.proposed: Apply Stewardship Code principles to unitholders exercising nomination rights
key_parameters.final: Stewardship Code principles made applicable to all unitholders holding 10% or more of outstanding units

notes: Board PR item 5.3-5.4 mirrors the anchor's Option 1 (10% threshold, collective nomination, Stewardship Code) almost word for word. Did not verify the gazetted InvIT/REIT Regulations amendment text for edge-case mechanics (e.g. exact clubbing procedure), hence content_label_confidence is medium.

decisive_document_title: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Foreign Venture Capital Investors) (Amendment) Regulations, 2024
content_summary: Roughly 16 months after the anchor consultation, SEBI notified the FVCI (Amendment) Regulations, 2024 on Sep 6, 2024 (effective Jan 1, 2025), shifting FVCI application processing and due diligence to DDPs -- who are empowered to grant the registration certificate on SEBI's behalf -- aligning the framework with the FPI regime, matching the anchor's central proposal. A search for an intervening SEBI board-meeting press release specifically approving this FVCI change did not find one (the Jun 27, 2024 board PR, PR No. 12/2024, does not mention FVCIs), so the gazetted amendment itself is used as the decisive document.

key_parameters.name: registration processing
key_parameters.proposed: Delegate FVCI registration/post-registration processing to DDPs, aligned with FPI framework; DDP=custodian
key_parameters.final: Adopted: applications made to a DDP, which reviews and grants the registration certificate on SEBI's behalf, aligned with the FPI framework

notes: This thread shows an unusually long consultation-to-action gap (~16 months) relative to most other threads in this sample, most of which were decided within the same year. Did not verify whether the demat-mandate and eligibility-criteria-review proposals were carried through unchanged, or fetch the gazette text itself, hence content_label_confidence is medium.
